Team — forwarding Halcyon’s ask. This is a strategic customer (large payments volume) and they want a carveout for a higher availability + tighter latency SLO than our public docs.

Quick context: they are offering a committed spend and co-marketing; Laura, please advise commercial flexibility. Markus

Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:22:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for 99.95% uptime & 95th <200ms latency commitment

Markus / team — engineering take: 99.95% is not impossible but it depends on deployment topology for their workload. Questions and constraints:

- Traffic shape: are they steady or spiky? Payment peaks at EOD can be 10x baseline.
- Model variant: small, quantized models vs larger ones; larger models have heavier tail latency.
- Regionality: do they require multi-region active-active? That’s the main lever to hit 99.95%.

Mitigations we will require to sign off on a contractual SLO:
- Active-active across two regions with cross-region failover (adds infra cost).
- Dedicated capacity or guaranteed pool sizing during windows (reserved nodes).
- Pre-approved fallback model (lighter, lower-quality but faster) and a strict runbook + automation for failover.
- Synthetic traffic SLO benchmark and monthly verified tests (we own the test harness).

I’ll draft a technical appendix we can attach to the SLA that enumerates failure modes and required entitlements. Estimated engineering lift: 3-4 engineer-weeks to produce a hardened config and automation for the pilot.

— Aditya
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:11:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for 99.95% uptime & 95th <200ms latency commitment

Markus / all — ops considerations: I agree with Aditya. To be comfortable operationally we need:

- A runbook (monitored playbook) with clear triggers for failover and escalation. I started a draft (runbook-draft-availability.md).
- Increased logging and retention for the pilot (14 days) to investigate incidents.
- A latency budget with explicit degradations (e.g., if CPU queued > X then auto-switch to fallback).
- SRE on-call rotation adjustment (estimated +0.6 FTE during pilot window) unless customer pays for premium support.

If we accept 99.95% without these, we’re exposing ourselves to high operational risk. Recommend tying acceptance to these preconditions and a 6-week pilot measured against synthetic and real traffic.

— Evelyn
Senior SRE

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 12:47:36 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for 99.95% uptime & 95th <200ms latency commitment

Team — commercial options: Halcyon has signaled they will commit to a 12-month reserved capacity with a monthly minimum spend that covers most infra delta. I can offer:

- Approval to proceed with the SLO subject to the technical appendix and runbook being finalized and legal review of the SLA language.
- A one-time onboarding credit to help offset automation work, and a premium support add-on billed monthly.
- We should require a periodic review clause (30/60/90 days) with objective gates to keep the SLO in place.

If engineering and ops accept the mitigation list, I’ll instruct contracts to draft the carveout language and include a pricing uplift.

— Laura
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts

From: markus.klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lo <sarah@halcyonpayments.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, contracts@halcyonpayments.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for 99.95% uptime & 95th <200ms latency commitment

Sarah — thanks for the patience. Internal alignment complete: Redwood can accept a pilot-level SLO of 99.95% uptime and a 95th percentile latency target of <200ms provided the following are contractually required:

1) Technical appendix (to be authored by Aditya) that lists deployment topology, fallback model, and synthetic test harness.
2) Active-active across two regions with reserved node pool during business hours.
3) Signed runbook and monthly synthetic verification (we will own test execution).
4) Premium support add-on and a pricing uplift to cover +0.6 FTE operational cost.
4) 6-week measured pilot with objective gates and a clause to revert SLOs if gates are not met.

Laura will push commercial language and contracts will draft the specific carveout. Aditya/Evelyn will iterate the appendix and runbook this week. Monica will provide Ops cost numbers for the contract.

If that sounds acceptable we can have contracts circulate a draft by next Tuesday and aim to have DocuSign executed for the pilot by Nov 16.

Best —
Markus
VP Commercial
Redwood Inference
